claims.statement: Verified fact: GS1 EANCOM covers the transaction sequence through invoice and remittance advice and supports automated reconciliation of supplier invoices with receipt information.
Verified fact: GS1's claims vocabulary includes promotion discounts, quantity discounts, incorrect references, and incorrect charges as adjustment reasons.
Hypothesis (unvalidated): despite standardized messages, mid-sized suppliers have enough unresolved promotion deductions to pay a case-resolution layer and share outcome labels.

contrary_evidence: GS1 already defines Commercial Dispute, Claims Notification, invoice, debit/credit, and remittance messages, so standard EDI and incumbents may be sufficient: https://www.gs1.org/sites/gs1/files/docs/eancom/ean02s4/part1/part1toc.htm
GS1 explicitly says buyers can automate invoice reconciliation with receipt information, reducing novelty in basic matching: https://support.gs1.org/support/solutions/articles/43000734250/

economics.acquisition_route: Offer a fixed-scope historical deduction audit through EDI/finance partners, then convert recurring accounts-receivable workflows.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: 8 brands at PLN 7,000 MRR in year 2, 25 at PLN 12,000 MRR in year 4, and 40 at PLN 15,000 MRR in year 6 imply PLN 7.2m ARR before recovery fees. At 25% owner earnings or a 3-4x ARR value and 65% ownership, PLN 5m net worth is plausible in years 4-6; absence of measurable incremental recovery in three audits invalidates success-fee economics.
economics.founder_time: 3-4 hours/day while piloting one retailer format; avoid using any employer-confidential information and recruit an independent FMCG finance adviser.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 65-82%; human dispute work can erode margin, so the product must automate evidence assembly and limit bespoke negotiation.
economics.payback: Unvalidated customer hypothesis: verified incremental recoveries exceed annual subscription by at least 3x; only a blinded historical audit can test this.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated estimate: PLN 4,000-18,000 monthly plus 3-10% of contractually verified incremental recoveries, with no fee on merely reclassified valid deductions.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Retailer deductions and promotions recur continuously; retailer-specific mappings and outcome history improve every cycle.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: retailer-specific reason-code mappings and outcome-labeled case patterns improve automation; agreement and claim history becomes the operational memory for renewals
fingerprint.customer: mid-sized CPG brands and distributors selling through Polish and Central European grocery, drugstore, and convenience chains
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: FMCG ERP/EDI consultancies, fractional finance leaders, distributors, and a paid historical-deduction recovery audit
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: EDI/email ingestion, promotion-term extraction, line-level claim matching, evidence assembly, workflow with sales, credit-note generation, and recovery analytics
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: supplier finance or revenue-growth team pays a subscription plus a fee when a deduction is resolved or cash is demonstrably recovered
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a retailer remittance arrives short or a debit note cites a promotion discount that finance cannot trace to agreement and sell-out evidence

founder_fit: The founder understands FMCG data and business processes, subject to strict separation from employer confidential information.
Document matching, causal checks, and exception classification use AI and quantitative skills.
A historical audit validates value before a large product build.
Partner-led B2B distribution avoids a public-facing creator strategy.
risks: Employer conflict-of-interest and confidentiality boundaries must be explicit and independently reviewed.
Retailers may not accept machine-generated dispute evidence or expose detailed reason codes.
ERP, trade-promotion-management, and EDI vendors may already address the workflow.

structure.control_point: promotion-agreement-to-remittance case file that determines whether a retailer deduction is accepted, disputed, credited, or recovered
structure.critical_dependency: access to retailer remittance/deduction detail, promotion terms, POS evidence, and stable product/location identifiers

thesis: Build a claims exchange for mid-sized FMCG suppliers and distributors that joins a promotion agreement, item and location master, sell-in/sell-out evidence, invoice, remittance advice, retailer deduction, credit note, and resolution. It starts supplier-side and charges when a deduction is classified, accepted, disputed with evidence, or recovered. The control point is the commercial-dispute case file, not forecasting or generic EDI transport.
title: FMCG Trade-Promotion Deduction Resolution Exchange
uncertainties: The recoverable deduction rate in the target midmarket is not established.
Retailer data formats and contractual dispute windows need validation.
It is unknown whether finance, key-account sales, or revenue-growth management owns budget.
The founder cannot rely on non-public employer data, contacts, or processes for validation.
